status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026, checked by the translation workers, and deployed to earthfluent.com on 13 November 2026. Informal ty throughout; a male speaker where the word shows it.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Letters with Tails and Strokes, Part 1
lessons.description: Polish adds marks to make new letters: ę and ą are said through the nose, ł sounds like an English w, and ó like oo. Hear ręka, są, mały, and góra.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Sz, Cz, and Rz, Part 1
lessons.description: Two letters, one sound: sz is sh, cz is ch, and rz is like the s in measure. Hear szkoła, czas, rzeka, and morze.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Soft Sounds, Part 1
lessons.description: A stroke over s, c, z, or n makes it soft, said with the tongue flat against the roof of the mouth. Hear coś, być, źle, and koń.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Where the Stress Falls, Part 1
lessons.description: Almost every Polish word is stressed on its second-to-last beat. Hear it in kobieta, samochód, dziękuję, and Warszawa.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb iść, to go, changes its ending to say who is going. Spot what changes: idę, idziesz, idzie, idziemy.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of iść, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are off to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: Polish has no word for the or a. For more than one, the ending changes, and sometimes the middle too: pies becomes psy.

lessons.title: Patterns - Words That Match, Part 1
lessons.description: A describing word matches the thing it describes, whether a he-word, a she-word, an it-word, or many: nowy, nowa, nowe, nowe.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: Put czy in front of a statement and it becomes a yes-or-no question. Nothing else moves.
words: This is the bus to Warsaw.
Is this the bus to Warsaw?
Czy to jest autobus do Warszawy?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: To say something is not so, put nie in front of the verb. Nothing else in the sentence changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Leaving Out I and You, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb's ending already says who is doing it, so Polish usually leaves out I, you, we, and they.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come First, Part 1
lessons.description: As in English, the describing word comes before the thing it describes, and matches it.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb iść, to go on foot, at work in whole sentences, and jechać, which Polish uses for going on wheels.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. A no takes nie twice: once for no, and once in front of the verb.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: Describing words matching what they describe, in whole sentences: biały, czerwone, wysoka, małe.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways. The verb changes for a trip finished, a trip under way, and a trip to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
